newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil still under pressure with offers.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil still under pressure with offers.

text.p: Singapore oil product prices remained weak on Wednesday despite a rise in crude values as sellers offered aggressively while buyers held back, traders said.

Traders said physical players ignored a $2.50-a-tonne rise in IPE gas oil as weak regional demand set the market tone. Three majors emerged to offer one million barrels of gas oil for end-January and early February lifting. A European major offered three cargoes at ever lower prices--$28.75 a barrel for Jan 30-Feb 3 lifting fob, $28.85 for Feb 2-6 and $28.80 for Feb 8-12. Another major offered at $29.05 but buyers were absent.

One trader said the bottom was not yet in sight as China has been absent while North Asian weather was curbing purchases. Traders said MidEast supplies could also start to pile up. Nepal bought in its tender for February arrival gas oil from Shell at $239.39 a tonne and kerosene from Mobil Corp at around $274.

Taiwan might sell a second gas oil cargo in its end-Jan early-Feb tender and was seeking around $29.50 for the first cargo. Naphtha was steady with Japan's absence for a holiday cutting direction. Swaps were unchanged with Feb at $24.20/$24.50, second-half March open-spec slightly lower around $240 a tonne.

The naphtha March crack has goen out more than $10 in past week to $69/t. But weaker sentiment was expected as export cargoes being offered out of India in January. Sellers said buyers were sidelined expecting softer crude prices, but up to four spot cargoes were heard available in Singapore in February.
